studyTitle: A Phase 2 Single-Arm, Multicenter, Exploratory Safety and Efficacy Study of IF001 to Remove Long-Term Immunosuppression from Prior Living Donor Kidney Transplant Recipients (RELIEF)
studyDesign: Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study

interventionalStudyDesign.description: Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study to demonstrate the safety and efficacy of IF001 in adult participants 3 to 62 months following transplantation of a kidney from a living donor

masking.description: Not applicable as this is an open-label study

arms.description: IF001 and initial tacrolimus plus MMF, with elimination of IS after 12 months

indication: kidney transplant recipients with stable renal allograft function who received a kidney transplant from a partially or fully HLA-matched living donor 3 to 62 months prior to signing informed consent
objective: to evaluate the proportion of recipients free from IS (without BPAR) 24 months post-transplant

studyArm.name: Single-arm IF001 treatment
studyArm.description: Adult participants 3 to 62 months following transplantation of a kidney from a living donor who will receive IF001 product generated from the same living kidney donor through G-CSF mobilization and apheresis

studyIntervention.name: Thymoglobulin
studyIntervention.description: Days −9 (0.5 mg/kg intravenously [IV] over 6 hours), −8 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours), and −7 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours); preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) other than Thymoglobulin are excluded

studyIntervention.name: Fludarabine
studyIntervention.description: Days −6, −5, −4, −3 and −2 (30 mg/m2 IV daily, dose adjusted for kidney function)

studyIntervention.name: Bacterial Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: Bacterial prophylaxis must be provided at least from Day 1 until the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is >500 cells/µL. Specific antibacterials may be given according to center practice. An example is moxifloxacin 400 mg per day.

studyIntervention.name: Fungal Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: Fungal prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until the ANC is >500 cells/µL. Specific antifungals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement but must include coverage of molds such as Aspergillus. An example is posaconazole 300 mg daily.

studyIntervention.name: Viral Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: Herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until Day 183 and is recommended until Month 12. Specific antivirals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement. An example is valacyclovir 500 mg twice a day.

studyIntervention.name: CMV Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: for participants who are immunoglobulin G (IgG) (+) for CMV and participants who are IgG (−) for CMV but who received a kidney from a donor who is IgG (+), it is recommended that CMV prophylaxis be provided from Day 1 until Day 92. Specific antiviral medications may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement. An example is letermovir 480 mg once daily.

studyIntervention.name: Pneumocystis Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: Pneumocystis prophylaxis (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia/pneumocystis carinii pneumonia) must be provided starting on Day 22 or after the ANC is >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 single strength tablet daily is the preferred example, with atovaquone 1500 mg once daily or dapsone 100 mg once daily as alternatives.

statisticalAnalysis.description: Statistical methods were not taken into consideration in determining the sample size. Because this is a proof-of-concept study, no hypothesis tests will be conducted on the primary safety endpoint. The primary safety endpoint will be summarized using a point estimate along with its 95% confidence interval (CI) (exact binomial). Because this is a proof-of-concept study, no hypothesis tests will be conducted on the key secondary efficacy endpoint.

concomitantMedications.name: Concomitant Medications
concomitantMedications.description: The investigator should instruct the participant to notify the study site about any new medications, including non-prescription supplements, he/she takes after study enrollment. All medications, procedures, and significant non-drug therapies (including physical therapy and blood transfusions) administered after the participant has signed the study informed consent form (ICF) will be recorded on the relevant case report form (CRF).

taperedBeforeBaseline.name: Prednisone or equivalent corticosteroid
taperedBeforeBaseline.description: If a participant was taking daily corticosteroids for >90 days prior to study enrollment, weaning of corticosteroids to prevent adrenal insufficiency is allowed per institutional standard or clinical judgement, provided that corticosteroids are withdrawn prior to Month 9.

prohibited.name: Preparations of ATG other than Thymoglobulin

dataMonitoringCommittee.name: data safety monitoring board
dataMonitoringCommittee.label: DSMB
dataMonitoringCommittee.description: An independent data safety monitoring board (DSMB) will oversee the safety and risk/benefit of the study. The DSMB will critically assess the sponsor and investigators on matters relating to the safety and conduct of the study.
dataMonitoringCommittee.mandate: will oversee the safety and risk/benefit of the study
dataMonitoringCommittee.charter: The DSMB will be governed by a charter that will include meeting frequency, stopping rules, and event triggers necessitating an unscheduled review

cellTherapyManufacturing.name: IF001
cellTherapyManufacturing.description: an investigational cell therapy product containing defined doses of CD34+ HSCs and αβ TCR cells for induction of transplantation tolerance in recipients of kidney transplants from the same donor
cellTherapyManufacturing.collectionProcedure: granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilization and apheresis
cellTherapyManufacturing.minimumStemCellYield: a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW
cellTherapyManufacturing.manufacturingNotes: The cryopreserved product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW (no maximum) and a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). Freshly harvested donor stem cells will be immediately transported to the manufacturing center where the IF001 product will be manufactured, cryopreserved, and stored prior to shipping to the study center for thawing and infusion into the participant.

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Reduced Intensity Conditioning Regimen
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: RIC regimen
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Nine days prior to IF001 infusion, participants will begin a reduced intensity conditioning regimen

agents.name: Thymoglobulin®
agents.dose: 0.5 mg/kg intravenously [IV] over 6 hours on Day −9, 2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours on Day −8, 2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours on Day −7

agents.name: Fludarabine
agents.dose: 30 mg/m2 IV daily, dose adjusted for kidney function

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.dose: 14.5 mg/kg IV daily on Day −6, Day −5

agents.name: Total body irradiation
agents.dose: 200 cGY for the HLA-matched cohort and 400 cGy for the partially HLA-matched cohort

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Acute GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Characterize the incidence and grade of acute GVHD by Day 120

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Chronic GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Characterize the severity of chronic GVHD by one-year post-IF001 infusion

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: CD34+ HSCs Collection
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: αβ TCR cells Collection
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg)
stemCellCollectionRequirements.rationaleForMinimum: The dose of 10 ± 2 million αβ TCR cells/kg in the RELIEF trial was chosen to minimize the incidence of severe acute or chronic GVHD while simultaneously reducing the incidence of graft failure and opportunistic infection
